name: Brook Byers
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Byers was working in entry-level roles (consulting, publishing, semiconductor finance) before joining Pitch Johnson's Asset Management as a VC apprentice in 1972 at age 27. Cofounded Kleiner Perkins in 1977 at age 32.
early_history_summary: Byers earned a BSEE from Georgia Tech in 1968 and an MBA from Stanford, then worked briefly at Management Analysis Corporation, Behavioral Research Laboratories, and Advanced Memory Systems before joining Pitch Johnson's venture fund in 1972.
evidence_summary: Byers grew up in Atlanta, Georgia, earned a Georgia Tech EE degree and Stanford MBA, then cycled through several early jobs before finding venture capital at age 27. His defining career milestone—cofounding Kleiner Perkins and pioneering biotech VC—came well after age 26. No material, dated milestone by 26 was found.

name: John Doerr
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Doerr joined Intel as an engineer/salesperson in 1974 at age 23 and was a strong performer, but his defining career milestone—joining Kleiner Perkins in 1980 and leading landmark investments—came at age 29.
early_history_summary: Doerr earned BS and MEE degrees in electrical engineering from Rice University and an MBA from Harvard in 1976. He joined Intel in 1974, working on the 8080 microprocessor and becoming a top-ranked salesperson before moving to Kleiner Perkins in 1980.
family_context_summary: Born in St. Louis, Missouri, one of five siblings; attended Chaminade College Preparatory School. Parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Doerr came to Silicon Valley in 1975 with engineering degrees from Rice and an Harvard MBA. He worked at Intel as an engineer and top salesperson, but his venture capital career and landmark investments (Netscape, Amazon, Google) began after age 26. No material, dated milestone by 26 was found.

name: Michael Moritz
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Moritz earned his Oxford history degree in 1976 and Wharton MBA in 1978, then worked as a journalist at Time magazine. His defining career milestone—joining Sequoia Capital in 1986—came at age 32.
early_history_summary: Moritz grew up in Cardiff, Wales, the son of Jewish refugees from Nazi Germany. He studied history at Christ Church, Oxford, earned an MBA from Wharton in 1978, then became a Time magazine reporter covering Silicon Valley before co-founding Technologic Partners and joining Sequoia in 1986.
family_context_summary: Born to a Jewish family in Cardiff, Wales; father Ludwig was a professor of Classics and later Vice Principal at Cardiff University; mother Doris also fled Nazi Germany. Both parents were refugees.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an academic (Classics professor at Cardiff University); no direct technology or business domain transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Moritz was the only pupil from his Cardiff comprehensive school to go to Oxford, then earned a Wharton MBA and became a Time reporter. His venture capital career at Sequoia and landmark investments (Google, Yahoo, PayPal) began well after age 26. No material, dated milestone by 26 was found.

name: Don Valentine
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Valentine graduated from Fordham, served in the military, and worked as a sales engineer at Raytheon. He joined Fairchild Semiconductor in 1959 at age 27, which launched his semiconductor and VC career.
early_history_summary: Valentine grew up in a working-class Catholic family in the Bronx, graduated from Fordham University, served briefly in the U.S. military (which brought him to California), then worked as a sales engineer at Raytheon before joining Fairchild Semiconductor in 1959 and later National Semiconductor.
family_context_summary: Born in the Bronx to a working-class Catholic family of Danish background; father worked on a milk route, mother was a homemaker who suffered from tuberculosis. Parents had limited formal education.
parent_family_domain_summary: No domain expertise transferred; working-class family with no technology or business connections.
evidence_summary: Valentine came from a working-class Bronx family, paid Fordham tuition quarterly in cash, and entered the semiconductor industry at age 27 via Fairchild. His founding of Sequoia Capital in 1972 and landmark investments (Apple, Oracle, Cisco) came decades after age 26. No material, dated milestone by 26 was found.

name: Pierre Lamond
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Lamond was completing his education (University of Toulouse, Northeastern University) and had not yet entered the semiconductor industry. His first job at Transitron Electronics began in 1957 at age 27.
early_history_summary: Lamond was born in France, studied electrical engineering at the University of Toulouse and earned a master's in physics there, then another master's in EE from Northeastern University. His first industry job was at Transitron Electronics in 1957, followed by Fairchild Semiconductor in 1961 and co-founding National Semiconductor in 1967.
family_context_summary: Born in France; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Lamond was still completing his engineering education in France and the U.S. through his mid-twenties. His semiconductor career began at age 27 at Transitron, and his defining milestones (Fairchild, National Semiconductor, Sequoia Capital) all came after age 26. No material, dated milestone by 26 was found.

name: Doug Leone
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Leone earned his Cornell BS in 1979 and was working in sales positions at Sun Microsystems, HP, and Prime Computer. He joined Sequoia Capital in 1988 at age 31 and became managing partner in 1996.
early_history_summary: Leone was born in Genoa, Italy, and moved to the U.S. at age 11, settling in Mount Vernon, New York. He earned a BS in mechanical engineering from Cornell in 1979, worked in technical sales at Sun Microsystems, HP, and Prime Computer, then earned MS degrees from Columbia and MIT Sloan before joining Sequoia in 1988.
family_context_summary: Born in Genoa, Italy; moved to the U.S. at age 11 with his parents, settling in Mount Vernon, New York. Father described as strong and funny, mother as shrewd and warm. Family was working-class; Leone describes himself as an outsider trying to blend in.
parent_family_domain_summary: No domain expertise documented; father's occupation not specified beyond general descriptions.
evidence_summary: Leone immigrated from Italy at age 11, earned engineering degrees from Cornell, Columbia, and MIT Sloan, and worked in tech sales before joining Sequoia at 31. His defining VC career and landmark investments came well after age 26. No material, dated milestone by 26 was found.

name: Roelof Botha
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Botha was completing his Stanford MBA (graduated 2000) and had not yet joined PayPal. He became PayPal's director of corporate development in 2000 at age 27 and CFO in September 2001 at age 28, leading the IPO in February 2002.
early_history_summary: Botha grew up in South Africa, earned a BSc in actuarial science from the University of Cape Town in 1996 (top GPA in university history), worked at McKinsey in Johannesburg from 1996 to 1998, then moved to Stanford for an MBA. He joined PayPal in 2000, became CFO in 2001, and led the 2002 IPO before joining Sequoia Capital in 2003.
family_context_summary: Born in Pretoria, South Africa; grandfather was Pik Botha, South Africa's foreign minister in the last years of apartheid. Family moved to Cape Town when he was six. Raised in Hout Bay, a suburb of Cape Town.
parent_family_domain_summary: Grandfather was a prominent political figure (foreign minister); no direct technology or business domain transfer documented, though family had high social status.
evidence_summary: Botha was a Stanford MBA student at age 26, having previously excelled academically at UCT and worked at McKinsey. His PayPal CFO role, the 2002 IPO, and his Sequoia Capital career all came after age 26. No material, dated milestone by 26 was found.

name: Peter Thiel
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Thiel graduated Stanford Law in 1992, clerked for Judge Edmondson (1992-1993), worked briefly as a securities lawyer at Sullivan & Cromwell, and became a derivatives trader at Credit Suisse. He founded Thiel Capital in 1996 at age 29 and co-founded PayPal in 1998 at age 31.
early_history_summary: Thiel was born in Germany, moved to the U.S. as an infant, and grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area. He studied philosophy at Stanford (BS 1989), founded The Stanford Review, then earned a JD from Stanford Law in 1992. After clerking and brief stints in law and derivatives trading, he returned to California in 1996 and co-founded PayPal in 1998.
family_context_summary: Born in Germany to German parents who brought him to the U.S. at age one; family lived in Namibia (1971-1977) before returning to the U.S. and settling in the Bay Area. Parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Thiel was a law clerk and securities lawyer at age 26, having studied philosophy and law at Stanford. His entrepreneurial milestones—founding Thiel Capital (1996), PayPal (1998), and Palantir (2004)—all came after age 26. No material, dated milestone by 26 was found.

name: Reid Hoffman
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Hoffman was completing his MSt in philosophy at Oxford (1993) and had not yet entered the tech industry. He joined Apple Computer in 1994 at age 27, co-founded SocialNet in 1997, and co-founded LinkedIn in 2002 at age 35.
early_history_summary: Hoffman grew up in Berkeley, California, the son of two attorneys. He attended the Putney School in Vermont, graduated from Stanford in 1990 with a BS in symbolic systems and cognitive science, then earned an MSt in philosophy from Oxford on a Marshall Scholarship. He joined Apple in 1994, worked at Fujitsu, co-founded SocialNet in 1997, and joined PayPal's board before co-founding LinkedIn in 2002.
family_context_summary: Born in Palo Alto, California, and raised in Berkeley; both parents were attorneys. Attended the progressive Putney School in Vermont for high school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were attorneys; no direct technology or business domain transfer documented, though professional family background provided educational resources.
evidence_summary: Hoffman was an Oxford philosophy student at age 26, having studied symbolic systems at Stanford. His tech career began at Apple (1994) and his entrepreneurial milestones—SocialNet (1997), LinkedIn (2002)—all came after age 26. No material, dated milestone by 26 was found.

name: Ken Howery
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded PayPal (originally Confinity) in 1998 at age 23, serving as the company's first CFO and helping raise over $200 million in private financing.
early_history_summary: Howery was born in Texas and graduated from Stanford University in 1998 with a BA in economics. At Stanford, he was managing editor of The Stanford Review, the student newspaper founded by Peter Thiel, whom he met there. The same year he graduated, he co-founded PayPal with Thiel, Luke Nosek, Max Levchin, and Elon Musk, serving as CFO from 1998 to 2002.
family_context_summary: Born in Texas; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond birth state. He is an Eagle Scout.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford network, Peter Thiel partnership, PayPal Mafia, dot-com wave
evidence_summary: Howery's path to PayPal ran through Stanford, where he met Peter Thiel through The Stanford Review and graduated in 1998. The same year, at age 23, he co-founded PayPal as its first CFO. The Stanford ecosystem, the Thiel partnership, and the dot-com wave were the dominant early advantages. Family background is not documented. His role as CFO during PayPal's growth, IPO, and $1.5B sale to eBay established his career trajectory.
starting_point: Born in Texas in 1975; family background not documented in reviewed sources. Attended Stanford University for economics.
current_position: Serving as 27th U.S. Ambassador to Denmark (assumed office November 2025); previously co-founder and partner at Founders Fund; net worth estimated in the hundreds of millions.

trajectory.event: Co-founded PayPal (originally Confinity) with Peter Thiel, Luke Nosek, Max Levchin, and Elon Musk, serving as the company's first CFO.
PayPal went public (February 2002) and was acquired by eBay for $1.5 billion (October 2002); Howery served as eBay's Director of Corporate Development until 2003.
Co-founded Founders Fund with Peter Thiel and Luke Nosek, a San Francisco-based venture capital firm.
Appointed U.S. Ambassador to Sweden by President Donald Trump, serving until January 2021.
Appointed 27th U.S. Ambassador to Denmark, assuming office in November 2025.

name: Luke Nosek
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded PayPal (originally Confinity) in 1998 at age 23, serving as VP of Marketing and Strategy and creating the company's 'Instant Transfer' product, its most profitable offering.
early_history_summary: Nosek was born in Tarnów, Poland, and emigrated to the U.S. with his parents at age three, settling in Glen Ellyn near Chicago. He learned programming on a TI99/4A and skipped grades in school. He earned a BS in computer engineering from UIUC in 1996, co-founded SponsorNet New Media with Max Levchin and Scott Banister while still in college (1995), worked as an evangelist at Netscape (1997-1998), then co-founded PayPal in 1998.
family_context_summary: Born in Tarnów, Poland; family emigrated to the U.S. in 1978 when Nosek was three, first to Austria then to the Chicago area. Father Roman worked at a nuclear power plant design office and later started a transport company; mother Danuta was a chemist at Castrol. Family initially struggled financially as immigrants.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a chemist and father an engineer/designer at a nuclear power plant; no direct technology entrepreneurship transfer documented, but parents had technical/professional backgrounds.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Early programming, SponsorNet, Netscape, UIUC ACM peers, PayPal Mafia, immigrant drive
evidence_summary: Nosek emigrated from Poland at age three to a working-class immigrant family near Chicago. He learned programming on a TI99/4A, skipped grades, and at UIUC met Max Levchin and Scott Banister through the ACM chapter. He co-founded SponsorNet in college (1995), worked at Netscape, then co-founded PayPal at 23 as VP of Marketing. His early programming reps, the UIUC peer network, and the dot-com wave were the dominant advantages. Family provided a computer despite financial constraints, and immigrant status created urgency.
starting_point: Born in Tarnów, Poland in 1975; emigrated to the U.S. at age three with parents who worked as an engineer and chemist, settling near Chicago in a working-class immigrant household.
current_position: Co-founder and partner at Gigafund; co-founder of Founders Fund; billionaire with net worth estimated at ~$1.3 billion; resides in the San Francisco Bay Area.

trajectory.event: Co-founded SponsorNet New Media with fellow UIUC students Max Levchin and Scott Banister while still in college.
Graduated from University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign with a BS in computer engineering.

Co-founded Gigafund, a venture capital firm focused on frontier technology investments including SpaceX.

name: David Sacks
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Sacks graduated Stanford in 1994, attended University of Chicago Law School, and briefly worked at McKinsey. He joined PayPal (Confinity) in 1999 at age 27 as COO, which was his first major tech role.
early_history_summary: Sacks was born in Cape Town, South Africa, and emigrated to Tennessee with his family at age five. He earned a BA in economics from Stanford (where he met Peter Thiel), then a JD from the University of Chicago Law School. After briefly working at McKinsey, he joined PayPal in 1999 as COO, staying through the eBay acquisition in 2002. He later founded Yammer (2008) and co-founded Craft Ventures (2017).
family_context_summary: Born to a Jewish family in Cape Town, South Africa; father was an endocrinologist; paternal grandfather immigrated from Lithuania and started a candy factory. Family moved to Tennessee when Sacks was five, and later to Silicon Valley.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an endocrinologist (medical professional); grandfather was an entrepreneur (candy factory). No direct technology domain transfer documented, though professional family background provided educational resources.
evidence_summary: Sacks was in law school or just finishing at age 26, having studied economics at Stanford and law at the University of Chicago. His tech career began when Thiel recruited him to PayPal in 1999 at age 27. His entrepreneurial milestones—PayPal COO, Yammer founder, Craft Ventures—all came after age 26. No material, dated milestone by 26 was found.
